EarthFlux: Land-Surface Energy and Water Fluxes from Earth Observation Data

Source: R/EarthFlux-package.R
EarthFlux-package.Rd

EarthFlux is an R package under active development that aims to provide a reproducible, testable and auditable workflow for estimating spatially distributed actual evapotranspiration (ETa) following the conceptual chain

$$\textrm{MODIS} + \textrm{METRIC} + \textrm{GWR} \rightarrow ET_a$$

where Earth observation data provide the land-surface state, the METRIC surface energy balance framework provides the physical core, and geographically weighted regression (GWR) is investigated as a way to represent spatially varying meteorological forcing.

Details

Development status. Version 0.1.0 is the first, experimental release. It provides the METRIC core physics as numeric functions, from net radiation to daily actual evapotranspiration; the meteorological forcing (weather station tables, quality control, reference evapotranspiration) and its regionalization over the working grid (representative station, global regression, inverse distance weighting and GWR); the internal MODIS preprocessing into the surface state; and the example scene cauquenes_modis. The integrated workflow earthflux() does not exist yet. Most METRIC formulations are candidates pending verification against the primary reference (Allen et al., 2007); the reference evapotranspiration (FAO-56, ASCE-EWRI 2005), the unit conversions and the MODIS product facts are verified. No result has been validated: EarthFlux is not for operational or scientific production use. The use of GWR for meteorological forcing is treated as a research hypothesis that has not been validated.

Design principles.

  • The physical core (METRIC) does not depend on any specific sensor. Sensor modules (MODIS first) convert products into standardised physical variables with documented units.

  • Spatial regionalisation of weather data (GWR) is an independent module.

  • Diagnostics are part of the result: physically anomalous values are flagged, never silently corrected.

  • No equation enters the code without a reference, units, assumptions, domain of validity and a verifiable test case.
